title: Tame trait invariant ring and Kummer polynomial presentation
statement: Let R and B be complete strictly henselian discrete valuation domains [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with characteristic-zero fraction fields and positive residue characteristics. Let R -> B be an injective finite algebra map [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Let a finite group H act on B by R-algebra automorphisms, and suppose |H| is a unit of R. Put A = B^H, the actual fixed subalgebra. Then A is a discrete valuation ring and strictly henselian. There exist n>0 dividing |H|, a uniformizer pi of A and a uniformizer tau of B such that [Frac B:Frac A]=n for the canonical fraction-field inclusion, n is a unit of A, tau^n=pi, and evaluation at tau induces an A-algebra isomorphism A[X]/(X^n-pi) -> B [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. No faithful-action or perfect-residue-field hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: ILO XVI 3.7, p.254, tame extension S prime -> T; algebraic steps 1-7 of lem-per-tame-trait-quotient-log-etale; Stacks Tags 09I3, 0325, 09EB, 09ER

proof.text: Put $A=B^H$, $K=\operatorname{Frac}R$, and $L=\operatorname{Frac}B$. The map $R\to B$ is injective by hypothesis. The invariant subring $A$ is an $R$-submodule of the finite $R$-module $B$, so [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] makes $A$ finite over $R$. Any finite set of $R$-module generators of $B$ also generates it over $A$. Thus both ring inclusions are finite. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] and [lem-weil-pbc-integral-maximal-contracts-maximal], the contraction of $\mathfrak m_B$ to $R$ is $\mathfrak m_R$. In particular, a uniformizer of $R$ has strictly positive valuation in $B$.

Extend the action to $L$ by $h(b/c)=h(b)/h(c)$, and let $G$ be its image in $\operatorname{Aut}_K(L)$. Then $G$ is finite, acts faithfully, and has the same fixed elements as $H$. Put $F=L^G$. The invariant-fraction-field assertion [lem-sfb-finite-invariant-fraction-field-lifting], applied to $A\subset B$, identifies $F$ with $\operatorname{Frac}A$. More explicitly, for fixed $x=b/c$, the product $d=\prod_{h\in H}h(c)$ is a nonzero element of $A$ and $xd\in B\cap F=A$. Apply [lem-wf-finite-field-action-fixed-degree] to the faithful group $G$: $L/F$ is finite Galois and $n=[L:F]=|G|$. The fibres of $H\twoheadrightarrow G$ are the cosets of its kernel, so $n\mid|H|$. Hence $n$ is prime to the positive residue characteristic $p$ and is a unit in $R,A,B$.

source.place: Tag 09I3 (lemma-galois-over-fixed-field); invariant denominator calculation supplied independently.

proof.text: Use the DVR valuation $v:L^\times\to\mathbf Z$ of $B$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. We have $A=B\cap F$. The subgroup $v(F^\times)$ contains a positive integer by step 1; let $e$ be its least positive integer. Integer division shows this subgroup is $e\mathbf Z$. Choose $\pi\in F$ with $v(\pi)=e$; the nonnegative-valuation criterion puts $\pi$ in $A$. In any nonzero ideal of $A$, choose $a$ of least valuation. For every other nonzero $b$ in the ideal, $v(b/a)\geq0$, so $b/a\in B\cap F=A$. Thus every ideal is principal. An element of $A$ is a unit exactly when its valuation is zero, and its nonunits form $(\pi)$. Therefore $A$ is a DVR. Also $B$ is the integral closure of $A$ in $L$: its elements are integral by step 1; if $x\in L$ integral over $A$ had negative valuation, its monic equation would have its leading term of uniquely smallest valuation, contradicting the valuation sum rule. Thus $x\in B$.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr) and Definition 00IE (definition-value-group); restriction of the valuation and the ideal calculation are written out here.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-local-product] to the finite $R$-algebra $A$. It is a domain, so it is a complete Noetherian local ring for its maximal ideal, which step 3 identified as $(\pi)$. The complete-pair theorem [lem-weil-pbc-complete-pair-henselian] makes $(A,(\pi))$ henselian. By the equivalence in [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-local-root-lifting], this includes the simple-root lifting formulation used in the item. The fraction field of $A$ has characteristic zero since it lies between $K$ and $L$.

Put $k=R/\mathfrak m_R$ and $k'=B/\mathfrak m_B$. The local map of step 1 embeds $k$ into $k'$. A finite set of $R$-generators of $B$ maps to $k$-generators of $k'$, so $k'/k$ is finite. Since $k$ is separably closed, [lem-kun-sep-closed-finite-extension-purely-inseparable] makes this extension purely inseparable. Consequently every $h\in H$ acts trivially on $k'$: for each $c\in k'$ some $c^{p^r}$ lies in $k$, and Frobenius is injective in a field. For any lift $b\in B$ of $c$, the element $|H|^{-1}\sum_{h\in H}h(b)$ belongs to $A$ and still reduces to $c$. Thus $A/(A\cap\mathfrak m_B)\to k'$ is surjective and injective. By step 3 its kernel ideal is $\mathfrak m_A$. Hence $k_A=k'$, which is separably closed by the hypothesis on $B$. Together with step 4 this proves that $A$ is complete and strictly henselian.

source.place: Purely inseparable residue extension; Reynolds averaging argument supplied independently.

proof.text: Apply [lem-exc-dvr-galois-degree-data] to $A\subset F\subset L$. Its integral closure is precisely $B$ by step 3, and $B$ is local. Thus the number of maximal ideals of the normalization is one. Step 5 gives residue degree one. The formula $[L:F]=g e f$ therefore reads $n=e$, so $\pi=u t^n$ for a uniformizer $t$ of $B$ and a unit $u\in B^\times$. This also verifies directly that the extension has ramification index prime to $p$, including when the action has a kernel.

The residue polynomial $X^n-\bar u$ has a root $\bar w\in k'$ because $k'$ is separably closed and $n$ is prime to $p$. Its derivative $n\bar w^{n-1}$ is nonzero. The given simple-root lifting property of $B$ supplies a unit $w\in B$ with $w^n=u$. Then $\tau=wt$ is a uniformizer and $\tau^n=\pi$. The hypotheses of [lem-sfb-totally-ramified-uniformizer-presentation] hold: $A$ is complete, $L/F$ is finite separable of degree $n$, $B$ is its local DVR integral closure, the residue fields agree, and $\mathfrak m_AB=\mathfrak m_B^n$. It follows that $B=A[\tau]$ and that the minimal polynomial of $\tau$ has degree $n$. Since the monic polynomial $X^n-\pi$ annihilates $\tau$ and has that degree, it is the minimal polynomial. We obtain the specified $A$-algebra isomorphism $A[X]/(X^n-\pi)\simeq B$, $X\mapsto\tau$.

source.place: Tag 09ER (lemma-weakly-unramified-goes-up-along-totally-ramified), first paragraph of its proof; simple-root lifting is an explicit hypothesis on B.

theorem tame_trait_invariant_kummer_presentation
    (R B : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing B] [IsDomain R] [IsDomain B]
    [IsDiscreteValuationRing R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing B]
    [IsStrictlyHenselianLocalRing R] [IsStrictlyHenselianLocalRing B]
    [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R]
    [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B) B]
    [CharZero (FractionRing R)] [CharZero (FractionRing B)]
    (hRchar : ringChar (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R) ≠ 0)
    (hBchar : ringChar (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B) ≠ 0)
    [Algebra R B] [Module.Finite R B]
    (hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap R B))
    (H : Type v) [Group H] [Finite H] [MulSemiringAction H B] [SMulCommClass H R B]
    (horder : IsUnit (Nat.card H : R)) :
    IsDiscreteValuationRing (FixedPoints.subalgebra R B H) ∧
    IsStrictlyHenselianLocalRing (FixedPoints.subalgebra R B H) ∧
    ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ n ∣ Nat.card H ∧
      @Module.finrank (FractionRing (FixedPoints.subalgebra R B H)) (FractionRing B) _ _
        (FractionRing.liftAlgebra (FixedPoints.subalgebra R B H) (FractionRing B)).toModule
          = n ∧
      IsUnit (n : FixedPoints.subalgebra R B H) ∧
      ∃ (pi : FixedPoints.subalgebra R B H) (tau : B),
        Irreducible pi ∧ Irreducible tau ∧
        tau ^ n = algebraMap (FixedPoints.subalgebra R B H) B pi ∧
        ∃ e : ((FixedPoints.subalgebra R B H)[X] ⧸ Ideal.span {X ^ n - C pi})
            ≃ₐ[FixedPoints.subalgebra R B H] B,
          ∀ Q : (FixedPoints.subalgebra R B H)[X],
            e (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ Q) = aeval tau Q
